  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commission

  SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any
Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a
catastrophe or emergency exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and need for action
thereon) arose within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot (except as stated) participate, it is requested that
all such communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a
member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to 3 minutes unless
such time limits are extended.

In the hybrid format, both in-person and hybrid audience members will participate in the following order:

Tier 1: In-person attendees

Tier 2: Teleconference attendees

Tier 3: In-person attendees who have not previously provided comments on the matter(s) being discussed by
the legislative body

Tier 4: Teleconference attendees who have not previously provided comments on the matter(s) being discussed

RECREATION
MANAGER UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda provided an update on the following
MANAGER ZEPEDA  programs and activities:

  1) She provided an update on her participation in the JEDI
  challenge from the California Parks & Recreation Society.
  2) A “Halloween Safety” flyer has been prepared and mailed out to

  all residents. She also acknowledged and thanked members of
  the Irwindale Police Department for organizing a Halloween
  Safety assembly on October 18.
  3) There are currently four Recreation Aides coaching the 24
  participants of the Flag Football program.
  4) The Cornhole League has been a big hit with ten teams of two
  participants each, and interested callers are inquiring when they
  could join.
  5) A Household Items Donation Drive will be held this Saturday by
  the Kindness Krew. Flyers with additional information are
  available. She thanked Recreation Aide Audrey Zepeda for
  creating the club.
  6) The members of the Tiny Tots and Teen Club have been asked
  to participate in the Senior Center Thanksgiving Dance to be
  held later this month.
  7) The Teeny and Tiny Tots enjoyed trips to Heritage Farms
  Pumpkin Patch in La Verne.
  8) The following trips will be held in the near future:
  A) Family Trip to San Clemente – November 19
  B) Day Camp trip to Universal Studios – November 22
  C) Family Trip to Disney on Ice – December 17
  D) Winter Day Camp trip to AMC Movie Theatre – December 27
  E) Winter Day Camp trip to Knott’s Berry Farm – January 3
  F) Teen trip to AMC Theatre – January 6
  9) The City Council recognized October as “Anti-Bullying Month”
  10) A Sunset Cinema double feature was held on October 14.
  11) The Teen Club members enjoyed a Halloween Party on October
  22.
  12) A Home Decorating Contest was held this month.
  13) Over 30 children participated in the Kids Pumpkin Decorating
  Contest held on October 27.
  14) The annual Halloween Spooktacular was held on October 29.
  The event was very successful thanks in part to the staff and
  volunteers that participated.
  15) Senior Recreation Leader Delicia Ponce worked hard to present
  the 2022 Jack O’ Lantern walk in October.
  16) A Trick or Treat Parade was attended by over 50 students of the
  Teeny Tots, Tiny Tots, and KidZone programs on October 31.
  17) Fifteen stops were added to this year’s Trunk or Treat activities
  held on Halloween night.
  18) The first Community Ofrenda is on display at the Dan Diaz
  Recreation Center through November 6.
  19) The Scarecrow Alley will take place November 21-26.
  20) The winter class schedule is currently being finalized and flyers
  will be mailed out soon.
  21) The following events have been scheduled for December:
  A) Christmas Spectacular and Mayor’s Tree Lighting – 12/2
  B) Teen Club Christmas – 12/16

  C) Teeny Tots Christmas – 12/21

AQUATICS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE

SUPERVISOR GRIJALVA Supervisor Grijalva provided an update on the following programs
  and activities:

  1) The Aquatic Center is now closed for the season and will reopen
  in March 2023, and will offer classes such as Aqua Stand Up,
  Mindful Waters, Senior Splash, Swim Team, Aqua Fitness, and
  Lap Swim programs.
  2) Last week, the Aqua-Fitness class concluded the fall session
  with a potluck dinner.
  3) The Swim Team competed against swimmers from Walnut,
  Duarte, and La Verne on October 19 at the La Verne Aquatic
  Center. Many Irwindale participants placed first and second.
  Participants ended the program recently with a banquet.
  4) Staff participated in the department trick or treat event for the
  Teeny and Tiny Tots.
  5) Aquatic Center management staff attended the 52nd Annual
  SCMAF Institute conference on October 6. While there, staff also
  attended the SCPPOA meeting of the month, with the next
  meeting to be held tomorrow at the new aquatic facility in Laguna
  Niguel.
  6) He reported that he also attended the California Aquatic
  Management School in Lake Arrowhead, where he enjoyed
  learning a variety of topics and was able to network with other
  professionals.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda commended Aquatics staff for their hard work and
  dedication.

MARIANA QUINONES  Mariana Quinones stated that she was very grateful that her children
  could enjoy the same programs that she enjoyed as a child, and
  thanked Supervisor Grijalva for being a great Supervisor.

ADAM QUINONES  Adam Quinones submitted a written message thanking Supervisor
  Grijalva and the Aquatics Division for their wonderful programs.

PUBLIC WORKS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE  Supervisor Rodriguez presented the following update:

  1) Trees were replanted at Jardin de Roca Park.

  2) Certain lawn areas were reseeded.
  3) The softball field was lined for the flag football season.
  4) The lighting at the gym floor has been repaired and retrofitted to
  LED.
  5) Staff is setting up for the Scarecrow Alley and the Veterans Day
  events. Holiday decorations will likely be set up after November
  11.
  6) Staff will attend pesticide training from November 15-17.
  7) He thanked staff for their hard work during the recent months, and
  commended staff from the Recreation and Aquatics divisions for
  bringing back wonderful activities and programs.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda thanked Pablo Gamez for the amazing job he did
  working as custodian at the recent Taste of Irwindale event.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE  Director Rodriguez presented the following update:

  1) Staff recently signed a contract with an engineering firm to design
  the concrete footings and to conduct certain repairs inside the pool
  pump room. The firm will also design the resurfacing of the deck
  so that new diving boards could be installed. Staff will continue to
  update the commission on the project.
  2) The city has partnered with the San Gabriel Council of
  Governments for its Energy Efficiency program, and staff is proud
  that Irwindale is the first city to have achieved the prestigious
  “Gold” level due to its commitment to energy conservation. Staff is
  working hard in an effort to reach the “Platinum” level in the future.
  3) Staff has pruned the palm trees as requested by Commissioner
  Ortiz.
  4) Staff continues working hard on the Irwindale Park Improvement
  Project. Staff is gathering the approved plans and specifications
  for Phases 4 and 5 to create and print the package required for
  the release of bids. Updates will be provided to the Commission
  as they develop.
  5) The annual holiday staff luncheon is scheduled for December 1.
  6) The Irwindale Library was recently awarded a $6 million grant from
  the state’s library grant program. She congratulated Librarian
  Shayna Balli and Assistant Engineer Luis Pimentel for
  collaborating to achieve the grant.
  7) The Irwindale Community Foundation will be offering gift cards to
  Irwindale residents on November 5, in collaboration with the
  Kindness Krew, which is soliciting household items for donation to
  a local non-profit organization.
  8) The January 2023 Parks & Recreation Commission meeting will
  be held on January 12.
  9) A Veterans Day Ceremony will be held on November 11.

DENA ZEPEDA  Dena Zepeda thanked Director Rodriguez for her leadership.

COMMISSIONER ITEMS
AND REQUESTS

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman thanked the staff and volunteers that
ROMAN  participated in the Halloween festivities and spoke about all the
  amazing city programs and events she enjoys. She also urged staff
  to continue attending educational seminars, and commended Public
  Works staff for being available seemingly at all hours of the day.

  Responding to a request by Commissioner Roman, Supervisor
  Rodriguez advised that the outdoor lighting at the Senior Center has
  already been upgraded to LED lights.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Sapien thanked staff of all community services
SAPIEN  departments for their wonderful work and indicated her eagerness to
  attend future events, such as the luau and paddleboard classes.
  She thanked the Public Works staff for their diligence, and
  requested to receive an update on the citywide camera program at
  the next meeting, to which Director Rodriguez briefly provided an
  update on the status, though she indicated that it will be further
  discussed at the December meeting.

  Commissioner Sapien also requested that the lighting near the bus
  stop in front of City Hall be improved, to which Supervisor Rodriguez
  advised that staff is looking to improve the lighting in the area by
  retrofitting the poles with LED lights. She also suggested that the
  new Library be named “Founding Mothers of Irwindale Library”, to
  which Director Rodriguez noted that the Council has formed an ad
  hoc committee to discuss the Library project.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Ortiz acknowledged the hard work of all staff in
ORTIZ  ensuring the success of city classes and functions. She added that
  she looked forward to spinning classes in the pool and noted the
  pool’s cathartic effects. She also appreciated the hard work of the
  Public Works staff.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo thanked staff for immediately addressing concerns
  brought up by the commissioners. She also thanked staff members
  of all departments for working hard to enact programs and functions
  that enrich the lives of so many. She also suggested that staff look
  into arranging collaborative activities between the city’s Aquatics
  Center and Northview High School’s Swim Team, to which
  Supervisor Grijalva indicated that staff is looking into partnering with
  several schools. She then thanked Director Rodriguez for keeping
  the Commission well informed and urged that staff work to ensure
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  NOVEMBER 2, 2022

  that the Irwindale Park Improvement Project not be conducted
  during peak activity season.

  Chair Fraijo asked about winterizing the lawn at the park, to which
  Supervisor Rodriguez indicated that staff will aerate the lawn and
  reseed with winter rye. She also thanked staff for the programs that
  are offered to the community, many of which may not otherwise be
  able to afford participating in them.

ADJOURNMENT  There being no further business to conduct, the meeting was
  adjourned at 7:22 p.m.
